description_good_justification: The README opens with what the library does: primitives for SSI libraries and applications, namely DIDs, key management behind a pluggable key store, and JWT-based verifiable credentials. It then lists every feature. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit#readme
interact_justification: Obtain: `cargo add identity-kit` from crates.io (https://crates.io/crates/identity-kit), as the README says. Feedback: bug reports and feature requests go to GitHub issues (https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/issues), linked from the README's Development section. Contribute: CONTRIBUTING.md, also linked there.
contribution_justification: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md: contributions are GitHub pull requests, squash-merged, with a Conventional Commits title. The file lists the checks CI runs on every pull request.
contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#checks: code must pass `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, the tests, rustdoc with `-D warnings`, `cargo hack` per feature, `cargo deny` and the layer-boundary build. It must respect the MSRV, and PR titles follow Conventional Commits.
documentation_basics_justification: The README covers features, Cargo features, key stores and how to extend the crate (new DID methods, key store backends). docs/DESIGN.md describes the architecture: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/docs/DESIGN.md
documentation_interface_justification: The API reference on docs.rs documents every public item; `missing_docs` is a lint and rustdoc runs with `-D warnings` in CI. Its examples are doctests. https://docs.rs/identity-kit
sites_https_justification: The project lives on GitHub (https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit), is distributed through crates.io (https://crates.io/crates/identity-kit) and documented on docs.rs (https://docs.rs/identity-kit), all HTTPS only.
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests (https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/issues). They are searchable, every topic and comment has a URL, anyone can join, and they work in a browser without proprietary software.
english_justification: All documentation, issues and reviews are in English.
maintained_justification: Actively developed: 50+ pull requests merged since October 2026, v0.2.0 released 2026-10-23, and Dependabot and security updates handled.
repo_track_justification: Git records who made each change and when. Every change to `main` is a squash-merged pull request with its review and CI history.
repo_interim_justification: All work happens in public branches and pull requests, merged into `main` between releases.
version_unique_justification: Each release has its own version (v0.0.2, v0.1.0, v0.2.0), published on crates.io, where versions can't be reused.
version_semver_justification: SemVer, following Cargo's SemVer rules; release-plz derives the next version from Conventional Commits and `cargo-semver-checks`. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/docs/RELEASE.md
version_tags_justification: Every release is a git tag (`vX.Y.Z`) with a GitHub release: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/tags
release_notes_justification: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog format, breaking changes marked). The same notes appear on each GitHub release: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/releases
release_notes_vulns_justification: No release has fixed a vulnerability with a CVE or similar identifier so far. SECURITY.md commits to publishing a GitHub Security Advisory and a RustSec advisory for any fix.
report_responses_justification: Every issue filed so far has been acknowledged and triaged (labelled, linked to its pull request), and most are fixed.
enhancement_responses_justification: Every enhancement request has been answered, and most were implemented, each linked to its pull request.
report_archive_justification: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/issues?q=is%3Aissue (open and closed issues stay public and searchable).
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports go through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting, which is enabled: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/security/advisories/new (described in SECURITY.md).
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports received so far. SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging a report within 14 days.
build_floss_tools_justification: The Rust toolchain and every dependency are FLOSS. `cargo deny` checks the dependency licences on every pull request.
test_justification: `cargo test --all-features` runs the unit tests, the doctests and 37 integration test files built on vectors from the W3C, IETF, DIF and DID method specifications. They're in the repository under Apache-2.0. CONTRIBUTING.md says how to run them.
test_most_justification: Coverage is measured with cargo-llvm-cov on every pull request and reported on Codecov: https://codecov.io/gh/impierce/identity-kit
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs the tests on Linux, macOS and Windows, the MSRV build, clippy, docs and the dependency checks on every pull request and on `main`: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/actions/workflows/qa.yml
test_policy_justification: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests: a pull request that adds or changes functionality adds tests for it, and a bug fix adds a test that fails without the fix, using the specifications' own test vectors.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent major changes each came with tests: KeyReference and KeyResolver (https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/pull/74), refusing SD-JWT payloads in JWT validators (https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/pull/85, tests/vc_sd_jwt_payload.rs), the RSA 2048-bit minimum (https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/pull/83) and the SD-JWT nesting limit (https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/pull/82).
warnings_justification: `[lints]` in Cargo.toml forbids `unsafe_code` and warns on `missing_docs`, `unreachable_pub`, `missing_debug_implementations` and several clippy lints. CI runs `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo hack clippy --each-feature -- -D warnings` and rustdoc with `-D warnings`.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI treats every warning as an error, so none can be merged.
warnings_strict_justification: All rustc and clippy warnings are errors in CI, checked for every feature on its own, and rustdoc warnings too. Unsafe code is forbidden.
crypto_published_justification: Only published, reviewed algorithms: EdDSA with Ed25519 (RFC 8032), ECDSA with P-256 and secp256k1, RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 and PSS, and SHA-2. They're used as specified by JOSE (RFC 7515, 7518, 8037), SD-JWT (RFC 9901) and VC-JOSE-COSE.
crypto_call_justification: The crate implements no cryptographic primitives. Signatures and hashes come from the RustCrypto crates (ed25519-dalek, p256, k256, rsa, sha2) and randomness from `getrandom`.
crypto_floss_justification: Every cryptographic dependency is FLOSS (MIT/Apache-2.0), checked by `cargo deny`.
crypto_keylength_justification: Keys the crate generates are Ed25519, P-256 or secp256k1, about 128-bit security. RSA keys shorter than 2048 bits are refused (https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/pull/83). These meet NIST's minimum through 2030.
crypto_working_justification: No MD4, MD5, single DES, RC4 or Dual_EC_DRBG anywhere. The `none` JWS algorithm is refused.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: SHA-1 isn't used, and no algorithm with known serious weaknesses is supported.
crypto_pfs_justification: The crate implements no key agreement protocol. TLS for did:web and the other HTTPS fetches is handled by the HTTP client (reqwest with rustls).
crypto_random_justification: Keys, SD-JWT salts and decoy digests come from the operating system's cryptographically secure generator through `getrandom` (e.g. 128-bit salts in `sd_jwt_vc::builder`).
delivery_mitm_justification: Distributed through crates.io over HTTPS. Cargo checks every download against the checksum in the crates.io index. GitHub releases also carry SLSA build provenance signed through Sigstore (https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/releases/tag/v0.2.0).
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is fetched over HTTP. Cargo and the release workflow use HTTPS only.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No known vulnerability affects the library. Two RustSec advisories are ignored, with the reason recorded in `deny.toml` and `osv-scanner.toml`: RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (Marvin attack in `rsa`), which concerns private-key operations, while this crate only verifies RSA signatures (docs/adr/0001-rsa-verification-only.md); and RUSTSEC-2026-0387 (`crypto-bigint` before 0.7.6), whose only remaining copy, 0.5.5, comes from a test-only dev-dependency and never ships in the crate. Dependencies are checked against RustSec on every Cargo change and daily (`cargo deny`), and by OSV Scanner through OpenSSF Scorecard.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerabilities have been reported. SECURITY.md describes how fixes and advisories are published.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials in the repository. The only private keys are the published examples from the specifications' test vectors, under tests/vectors. Release credentials are short-lived: crates.io trusted publishing through OIDC, plus a GitHub App key held in GitHub secrets.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (Rust and GitHub Actions, `security-extended` queries) and clippy run on every pull request and every push to `main`: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/actions/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's `security-extended` query suite looks for common vulnerabilities.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: No open medium-or-higher findings. CodeQL alerts are triaged on each pull request and fixed before merging.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and push to `main`, and weekly.
dynamic_analysis_justification: 11 cargo-fuzz targets cover the parsers and validators. They run for one minute on pull requests that touch `src/`, and for ten minutes nightly: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/fuzz/README.md
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The crate is pure Rust with `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The fuzz targets build with debug assertions and overflow checks (cargo-fuzz's default) and assert their own invariants, such as round-trips. The tests run with debug assertions on.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No open findings. Any crash found by fuzzing is fixed before merging, with the input kept as a seed.
